name: Slow kicker
blurb: A lump with one odd atom. The odd atom grabs a neighbour, the bond stores a kick, and when the bond lets go the kick shoves the body one way and the light atom the other. The water stops the light atom faster than the heavy body, so the body gains ground on every beat. You can count the beats.

name: Four-atom swimmer
blurb: The smallest and thriftiest swimmer found: three of one type and one of another. It goes furthest per unit of energy of anything in the search.

name: Buzzer
blurb: The fastest body found. It beats too quickly to see, and burns energy about ten times faster than the slow kicker to go twice as fast. The search finds this first if speed is all you ask for.

name: Slipstream swimmer
blurb: This water has no splash at all: drag does not grow with speed. The only thing this body can use is that atoms in a row shield each other from the water. That is how real cilia work, and here it is weak but real.

name: Splash swimmer
blurb: This water has splash and no slipstream. A fast stroke meets much more resistance than a slow return, and that difference is the whole engine.

name: Raft
blurb: A larger body with several kickers firing along it. Try pulling atoms off to see how much of it the motor needs.

name: Darter
blurb: A quick four-atom swimmer. It is here mainly as the partner of the control below: same atoms, same rules, different water.

name: Control: plain water
blurb: The darter again, in water with plain drag only. It beats just as hard and goes nowhere. With plain drag the pushes and pulls inside a body always cancel, so nothing can ever swim. Every universe worth playing in needs splash or slipstream.

name: Membrane ring
blurb: A closed ring of one atom type that links only to its own kind, twice. Three loose atoms start inside and sixteen outside. Watch whether the insiders stay in and the outsiders stay out as everything jiggles. Try dragging an outsider through the wall, or dropping atoms inside.

name: Bag with a motor
blurb: The same kind of ring with a motor attached. The ring was placed by hand; the search found a motor that can push it and rules under which the ring stays closed while it is dragged along.

name: Second cell
blurb: Another cell from a different run of the search. The membrane is a floppy chain with no stiffness of its own, so it trails like a bag. Something inside pushing outward would round it out.

name: Foam
blurb: Nothing placed by hand: 260 atoms scattered at random. These rules knit them into a net of closed compartments on their own. About one random universe in twenty does this, almost always with one or two atom types.

name: Restless clusters
blurb: Random atoms that clump into clusters which keep making and breaking bonds without ever settling or blowing up. This is the most common kind of universe with bonds: about four in ten.

name: Gliders (one-sided forces)
blurb: No bonds here. Instead forces are one-sided: A chases B while B ignores A. Clusters glide around at once, with no beating and no energy bill. It is lively, but motion is free, so there is nothing for a player to earn.
